candidates.economic_channel: Liquidity providers temporarily withdraw and replenish displayed native depth at a fixed price after displacement. Potential advantage would come from transient inventory pressure resolving; book replenishment is not signed transactions and does not guarantee reversion. Require an expected move exceeding measured ticket costs before enrollment.
candidates.novelty: Fixed-price displayed quantity state is different information from all price/body/covariance/duration/spread-area/factor exacts. No claim of universally new microstructure taxonomy. Existing technical DOM receipt is not an enrolled DEVELOPMENT price response.

candidates.economic_channel: A server-resting native limit order may earn compensation for inventory/adverse-selection risk and avoid part of active reaction latency. Positive quoted width after fees is only an optimistic opportunity ceiling. Opening opposite CFD positions does not by itself harvest spread; liquidation, execution sequence and adverse selection must be measured.
candidates.novelty: Execution and inventory-compensation channel, not another return predictor or exit-only rescue of a closed exact. Quote-side trigger studies do not identify a server-resting versus active-client latency advantage.

candidates.economic_channel: New information may accumulate in an economically matched open instrument while another is authentically closed. A delayed target repricing beyond both-leg costs is only plausible with point-in-time native relation and closure authority; calendar proxies and generic return correlations do not supply it.
candidates.novelty: Only a closure-conditioned common-product information channel could distinguish this from generic lead-lag, factor drift and closed cash-futures exacts; if it does not, reject rather than relabel.
